market_question: Will Bitcoin dip to $35,000 in May?
reasoning: Historical monthly drawdowns exceed 60% roughly once every few years (e.g. Mar 2020, Apr 2013). Tail-risk models and fat‑tailed return distributions suggest ~0.5% per month probability of such a crash, whereas the market implies only ~0.2%. The market appears to be underpricing this deep‑tail binary event.
evidence_points: March 2020 saw a ~60% intra‑month peak‑to‑trough drop, showing such events are possible even in modern markets.
Bitcoin monthly returns exhibit excess kurtosis; a 4.5‑sigma move occurs more often than a normal distribution would suggest.
Alternative tail‑index estimates (e.g. t‑distribution with 3 df) put a 60% drawdown probability near 0.5–1% per month.
sources_consulted: Knowledge of fat‑tailed‑return distributions for crypto assets
